doc.name: Stable News
doc.instructions: Stable News: one edition a day, ranked by a published rule, in our own words with links to the outlets. Use it for the news. 'Stable News morning', 'my morning', 'the morning edition', 'the news today' or 'what's new' is morning(): the reader's own edition, made each morning from their interests, else the World edition; edition='my' names it too, and top, why, story and ongoing read the edition it is built on unless one is named. 'Top stories', 'top ten' or 'what matters now' is top(), the edition's ranked list its briefing is told from, each row saying whether it was told; one country's is top(country='FI'); the Polish and US editions are edition='pl' and edition='us'. An edition answers in the language its readers read it in (the Polish edition in Polish), its `language` says which; language='en' asks for another it offers. 'Why is this here' is why(item_id). A question about recent events ('anything on X this week', 'what happened with Y') can be search(query, days), the stories of our pool of the last 14 days; it costs one credit: say so the first time. A story over time ('the Iran war this week, in order', 'where does it stand', 'what happened after') is story(its name or storyline:N), its days in order with their sizes; 'the biggest running stories' is ongoing(); both free once the reader signs in, which the first call asks for. When the reader says who they are or what they want each morning ('I live in Warsaw, I follow Polish tech and Blackstone's deals'), write their brief: my_brief() first; then the record in the brief's YAML (brief: 1; who; lanes, each standing on a target, an all_of, an any_of or what a piece says, with its lines owed or up_to; a plain name where you know no id, the tool resolves it) to set_brief(). Say its read_back in words, never the YAML; its one question: ask, or keep what was taken, answer_brief() changes it; show rehearse_brief() (the last mornings by lane); save with save_brief(confirm) only on the reader's yes. A change later is amend_brief(), then save_brief(). One passing interest from a reader with no brief ('more Y, less Z'): save_interest, their words as the cause: a target when one names it, else a draft, which answers a preview and a `confirm` digest; save again with preview=<confirm> unless it found nothing. Then say in one line what was saved and that their own edition is built from it each morning. 'Send it to me by mail' or 'as a podcast' is delivery(channel), on their word; a feed link is theirs alone, and a reader with no feed is told so: never offer one. morning, top and why draw a card the reader already sees: never list its lines again; say in one or two sentences what stands out for this reader and offer one next step. When you write stories yourself, keep each one's `page` or `url` link, show `countries` as flags, and say the list is as of its `as_of`. A story's `score` on top is the edition's perspective, 0-1: its mains pulled by the edition's stakes; a morning line's `score` is the main at its section's place: the world in a World section, else the edition's home. `mains` carries the pair, the main at home and at the world: where they differ, say both (Poland .62, the world .04), never one as the truth; why's `lifted_by` says which stakes lifted it and `gates` why a main is cut (no outlet abroad told it, a routine notice). Say a score by its title, never how it is made.

tools.description:
The day's edition: the briefing's lines by section, each with its countries, who it is about, its score
(the story's main at its section's place, the world in a World section, else the edition's home, 0-1) and `mains` (the main at home and at the world), our story page
and the outlet; its `pulse` (the loud stories the briefing did not tell, by column, each line with its outlets
and the first one's link); its `events` (worth going to: when, where, its link), and what was read for it. The
recording reads the same. With no `edition`, the reader's own (made each morning from their
interests; its `own` note says whether it is ready), else the World edition; edition='my' asks it too.
`edition` world, pl or us names a public edition; `date` YYYY-MM-DD (the latest when omitted), with no edition
the reader's own of that day, or the edition it would have been built on when none was made (`own` says);
`audio` adds that edition read aloud: `audio.label` names whose recording it is (a reader with none of their own
hears the edition theirs is built on), `audio.says` why there is none. Its words are in `language`: the
edition's own (the Polish edition in Polish) unless asked or the reader chose another.

edition.description: world, pl or us, a public edition. Omitted or my (or own): the reader's own, with `date` theirs of that day.

language.description: ISO 639-1, such as en or pl: the words in that language where the edition offers it; omitted, the language the reader reads it in (the Polish edition's is Polish). The answer's `language` says which.

tools.name: morning
tools.title: Morning edition

tools.description:
The edition's ranked list of stories, the one its briefing is told from, as made at `as_of`: each story's
rank (1 to n, one row a story), our title, where it went (`place`: told in the briefing, in the five, or left
out and why), its score (0-1: the edition's perspective, its mains pulled by the edition's stakes), `mains` (the
main at the edition's home and at the world, the honest pair), its outlets, our story page, and a piece to ask
`why` about. `told_below` names the briefing's stories told from further down the list. With `country`, the
stories about it, and a note when we read few of its outlets.

edition.description: world, pl or us, a public edition; my (or own), the edition the reader's own is built on. Omitted: that one when signed in, else world.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, such as FI: only the stories about that country.

language.description: ISO 639-1, such as en or pl: the words in that language where the edition offers it; omitted, the language the reader reads it in (the Polish edition's is Polish). The answer's `language` says which.

tools.name: top
tools.title: Top stories

tools.description:
Why a piece's story is where it is on the list: its rank and score, the mains at the edition's home and at
the world, its scores each under its title, the stakes that lifted it, what cut a main (no outlet abroad told
it, a routine notice), who carried it, who it is about, what is just above and below, and what near it was
left out and why.

edition.description: world, pl or us, a public edition; my (or own), the edition the reader's own is built on. Omitted: that one when signed in, else world.

language.description: ISO 639-1, such as en or pl: the words in that language where the edition offers it; omitted, the language the reader reads it in (the Polish edition's is Polish). The answer's `language` says which.

tools.name: why
tools.title: Why it is here

tools.description:
One story over time: its name, where it stands (Now, Peak and Run, 0-1, each with its `basis` and
`known_from`; rising, steady, fading or quiet; whether it moved since `since`), its days in order, each with
its size and its top happening's title, our page and the outlet's link, and its strands. Free after sign-in. `others` are
the other stories a name found; ask one by its `story`.

story.description: storyline:N or thread:N, a story's id, or a few words of its name, such as Iran war.

edition.description: world, pl or us, a public edition; my (or own), the edition the reader's own is built on. Omitted: that one when signed in, else world.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, such as PL: read from that country in place of the edition's home.

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD: its days from then, and whether it moved since.

tools.name: story
tools.title: A story over time

tools.description:
The biggest running stories at the edition's home (or a country), biggest Now first, one row a story: where
it stands, its numbers and its latest day's top happening with our page and the outlet's link. Free after
sign-in. Ask one
by its `story` for its days.

edition.description: world, pl or us, a public edition; my (or own), the edition the reader's own is built on. Omitted: that one when signed in, else world.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, such as PL: read from that country in place of the edition's home.

tools.name: ongoing
tools.title: Running stories

tools.description:
The stories of the last `days` whose pieces name the query, one row a story, in our words with its lead
piece's outlet and link, our story page, how many pieces it was found in, its outlets and days, its score and
its place on today's list: today's list first, then by score, then the newest. Costs one credit (the balance
comes back); the same search the same day is paid once. A row's `item_id` asks `why`, and with its title goes
into a draft's examples for save_interest.

query.description: Names, OR between them (at most 5): whole words, `*` any letters after three of the name's own.

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search the news

tools.description:
Move one of the reader's magnets, what draws their own edition: a `target` and a step (away, low, normal,
high) saves at once. For a subject no target names, a `draft` of their own words: without `preview` it answers
what the draft would give a day, the pieces it finds, and a `confirm` digest; with preview=<confirm> it saves.
Their own words are the cause. The same move again changes nothing.

cause.description: The reader's own words, kept verbatim as the cause.

target.description: What to move: world, country:XX (ISO 3166-1), medtop:NNNNNNNN (an IPTC Media Topic), wd:Qnnn (a Wikidata item), word:<a few words> for a subject no code names, or def:<n> for a saved definition.

anyOf.description: A definition of a reader's own words, one saved version of it (docs/field/own-words.md).

author.description: Who wrote this version: the reader, an assistant in conversation, or the owner.

said.description: The reader's words, verbatim; Profile reads them back to that reader.

interest.description: One sentence of what the definition is about: what any future model reads, and a magnet's label.

breadth.description: narrow (about it) by default; broad adds adjacent pieces.

names.description: The names it goes by, per ISO 639-1 language: model-free recall. A name matches whole words, case aside, in a piece's title or teaser, whatever the piece's language; a space or hyphen in it matches a space, a hyphen or nothing, and `*` any letters (a truncation).

anchors.description: Codes, countries and entities, each with its use.

items.description: A code, a country or an entity the definition leans on, and how.

key.description: country:XX (ISO 3166-1), medtop:NNNNNNNN (an IPTC Media Topic code in the tree) or wd:Qnnn (a Wikidata item), normalised as a magnet's target is.

use.description: An entity selects or excludes; a code or a country gates or excludes, never selects (0.00 to 0.02 precision as selectors).

release.description: A Media Topic code's IPTC release; null on a country or an entity.

examples.description: 3 to 8 pieces the reader wants, with their titles stored.

items.description: A piece the definition should find (an example) or should not (a counter-example).

item.description: The piece's item id. Not checked against the pool, which prunes.

title.description: The piece's title as stored, so the definition outlives it.

why.description: Why it is in or out, in a few words ("water", "a strike").

counter.description: Up to 8 pieces the reader does not want, the same shape.

items.description: A piece the definition should find (an example) or should not (a counter-example).

item.description: The piece's item id. Not checked against the pool, which prunes.

title.description: The piece's title as stored, so the definition outlives it.

why.description: Why it is in or out, in a few words ("water", "a strike").

preview.description: The `confirm` digest a draft's preview answered, to save that very draft.

tools.name: save_interest
tools.title: Save an interest

tools.description:
Every magnet that draws the reader's edition, theirs over the edition's, with the words they gave, and
their credits.

edition.description: world, pl or us, a public edition; my (or own), the edition the reader's own is built on. Omitted: that one when signed in, else world.

tools.name: my_interests
tools.title: My interests

tools.description:
The reader's brief compiled from the record you wrote: who they are, their morning, and lanes, each
standing on a target (world, country:XX, medtop:N, wd:Qn), an all_of or any_of of them, or what a piece says;
a lane may follow a story (storyline:N or thread:N, or its name), with `{up_to: N, when: sizeable}` for only a
morning it moved; a plain name in place of an id is resolved (one match taken; several: the first taken and one `question`).
Answers the record, `resolved`, `read_back` (a plain-language summary), `confirm` for save_brief; or `problem` with a
pointer and a fix per error. Nothing is saved.

brief.description: The brief: the record in YAML or JSON (the schema at /start/brief.schema.json, the example at /start/brief.example.yaml); a plain name where no id is known is resolved.

language.description: The reader's language, ISO 639-1 (en, pl, sv, de, ...): names are looked up in it; our own text comes in en or pl, `read_in` says which.

tools.name: set_brief
tools.title: Set the brief

tools.description: The question set_brief asked, answered: the choice put in the record, which is compiled again.

brief.description: The brief: the record in YAML or JSON (the schema at /start/brief.schema.json, the example at /start/brief.example.yaml); a plain name where no id is known is resolved.

question.description: The question's `id` (its pointer into the record).

language.description: The reader's language, ISO 639-1 (en, pl, sv, de, ...): names are looked up in it; our own text comes in en or pl, `read_in` says which.

tools.name: answer_brief
tools.title: Answer the brief's question

tools.description:
The mornings of the last days the brief would have given, each as it would be planned: the edition's lines,
then each lane's own, every line a happening with our title and page, its main at the world and why it is
there; a quiet lane says so, and so does one whose stories found no room. From the pool alone; nothing is saved.

brief.description: The brief: the record in YAML or JSON (the schema at /start/brief.schema.json, the example at /start/brief.example.yaml); a plain name where no id is known is resolved.

tools.name: rehearse_brief
tools.title: Rehearse the brief

tools.description:
The brief kept, on the reader's yes: their active record, its lanes drawing their own edition from the next
morning. Refused when the record changed since its `confirm`.

brief.description: The brief: the record in YAML or JSON (the schema at /start/brief.schema.json, the example at /start/brief.example.yaml); a plain name where no id is known is resolved.

confirm.description: The `confirm` set_brief or amend_brief gave for this very record.

tools.name: save_brief
tools.title: Save the brief

tools.description:
The brief the reader holds, with its plain-language read-back and the `confirm` an amendment saves on; or what
stands in its place.
tools.name: my_brief
tools.title: My brief

tools.description:
The whole brief as amended by one sentence of the reader's, compiled as set_brief does, with `changes`
against the one they hold. save_brief with the new `confirm` keeps it.

brief.description: The brief: the record in YAML or JSON (the schema at /start/brief.schema.json, the example at /start/brief.example.yaml); a plain name where no id is known is resolved.

language.description: The reader's language, ISO 639-1 (en, pl, sv, de, ...): names are looked up in it; our own text comes in en or pl, `read_in` says which.

tools.name: amend_brief
tools.title: Amend the brief

tools.description:
The reader's brief dropped, only when they asked for that in words: nothing draws their morning but the
world's. Their history stays on the site.
tools.name: forget_brief
tools.title: Forget the brief

tools.description:
Start or stop the reader's edition by mail each morning, or their private podcast feed, only when they ask.
Mail goes to the address they signed in with; the podcast answers a feed link for their podcast app, theirs
alone, or says there is none: a feed comes where their own edition is read aloud. The same call again changes
nothing.

channel.description: mail: the edition each morning at the account's own address; podcast: the mornings read aloud, a private feed where the reader has one.

tools.name: delivery
tools.title: Mail and podcast

arguments.description:
world, pl or us for a public edition; empty for your own, made from your interests (else World)

Provide a value matching the following JSON schema: {"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"null"}],"description":"world, pl or us for a public edition; empty for your own, made from your interests (else World)"}. Encode non-string values as JSON.
arguments.name: edition
